faq.q: What is the best calorie tracker app in 2026?
faq.a: It depends on what you need. For most people who want a lasting habit without guilt, we recommend Fimbl, because it pairs quick logging with hunger and feelings check-ins and an optional numbers-free Calm mode. Cronometer is the best choice for detailed micronutrients, MacroFactor for adaptive macro targets, and MyFitnessPal for the largest food database.

faq.q: Which calorie counter has a free barcode scanner?
faq.a: As of October 2026, Fimbl, Cronometer, YAZIO and Lifesum include barcode scanning in their free versions. MyFitnessPal moved barcode scanning to Premium in 2022, and Lose It! lists it as a Premium feature in its App Store description.

faq.q: Is there a calorie tracker without ads?
faq.a: Fimbl has no ads in either its free or Premium version. MacroFactor never uses ads but has no free tier, and Lifesum and Cal AI list no ads. MyFitnessPal, Cronometer, Lose It! and YAZIO show ads in their free versions and remove them with a paid plan.

faq.q: Can I track what I eat without seeing calories?
faq.a: Yes. Fimbl's Calm mode (Premium) replaces calorie numbers with gentle A to C grades for how well each meal served your goals, hunger and mood, while it keeps counting quietly in the background. You can switch back to numbers at any time. None of the other apps in this comparison document a comparable mode.

faq.q: What is a good alternative to MyFitnessPal?
faq.a: On iPhone, Fimbl is a good alternative if you want free barcode scanning, no ads and a calmer, feelings-aware diary. Cronometer suits people who want micronutrient detail, and YAZIO suits people who want a large European food database on Android as well as iPhone.

faq.q: Is calorie counting bad for your mental health?
faq.a: For many people it's a useful, neutral tool. Some studies link calorie-tracking apps with more eating concern in certain users, while a randomised trial in low-risk students found no increase in eating-disorder risk. If tracking makes you anxious, a numbers-optional approach can help, and if food feels overwhelming, please talk to a healthcare professional.
